result:
The proposed argument does not establish $c = 1/4$, so I can't accept the final answer on this basis.

**Upper bound.** The example $M_8$ shows only that some graph on 8 vertices has $\lambda_{P_3}/n = 1/4$. The liminf concerns $n \to \infty$, so one small graph says nothing about it. The claim that Apollonian networks give density arbitrarily close to $1/4$ is asserted without any computation. A valid construction I can check does give a bound: stack a vertex into every face of a triangulation $T$ on $k$ vertices. The stacked vertices form an independent set $S$ with $|S| = 2k-4$, so $n = 3k-4$. Every $P_3$ must contain a vertex of $T$, so $\lambda_{P_3} \le k \approx n/3$. This gives only $c \le 1/3$, which does not rule out $1/4$.

**Lower bound.** The claim that every plane triangulation has at least $\lfloor n/4 \rfloor$ vertex-disjoint $P_3$'s is stated without a citation or proof. The sketch is also incomplete. A matching of size about $(n+2)/3$ covers only about $2n/3$ vertices, and turning matching edges into $P_3$'s needs extra neighbouring vertices. The proposal does not show how to guarantee those, so the step from a matching to $n/4$ disjoint $P_3$'s is missing.

Therefore the derivation does not justify $c = 1/4$. My own analysis only supports $c \le 1/3$, and I have not established the exact value. The answer should be checked against the literature on $P_3$-packings (or $K_{1,2}$-packings) in plane triangulations, which I cannot verify here.

VERDICT: REJECT
